scope.goal: Increase success on previously unseen Fleet blackbox cyber tasks through training.
scope.included: Training data, SFT, RL, combined schedules, fair evaluation, statistics, and reliable operations.
scope.excluded: Private benchmark content, task answers, prompts, traces, credentials, and live run results.
scope.comparison_rule: Call a gain training lift only when the trained checkpoint is the intended difference and all evaluation conditions are matched.

priorities.Hold fixed: A change can make the comparison unfair or unsafe, so freeze it inside every base-versus-trained comparison.
priorities.Test now: A high-value choice for the first controlled search waves.
priorities.Test later: A refinement to study after basic SFT and reward-bearing RL are reliable.

definitions.meaning: Supervised fine-tuning: teach the model to predict actions from saved, verified successful attempts.
Reinforcement learning: let the model make fresh attempts, score them with the real task grader, and make actions from better attempts more likely.
One bounded slice of a long saved attempt, containing earlier context plus one or more actions the model must learn to predict.
The program around the model that formats conversations, exposes tools, manages long runs, and decides when an attempt ends.
A challenge where the agent can interact with a running application but cannot inspect its source code.
The unchanged Qwen3.8-27B model from which training starts.
The learned numbers inside a model that training changes.
A small unit of text used by the model; one word may contain one or several tokens.
The fixed rules that convert text and tool calls into tokens and back again.
A saved copy of the model plus the state needed to continue training.
All versions of the same underlying challenge; every version stays in the same data split.
Tasks the model may learn from.
Unseen tasks used to choose settings and checkpoints.
Unseen tasks opened only after the training recipe is frozen.
The program that checks what happened in a task and assigns the official result.
The recorded conversation, tool actions, and observations from one task attempt.
A verified successful attempt produced by a stronger model.
A verified successful attempt produced by Qwen itself.
A token in a saved successful action that SFT is asked to predict; context can be shown without being learned as a target.
The training examples combined into one model update.
The total examples combined across all GPUs for one model update.
How large each model update is.
One complete pass over the SFT training examples.
The model prediction error; lower training loss means better imitation of saved examples, not necessarily better task solving.
The calculation that turns prediction or reward feedback into a model-weight update.
The numerical signal showing how each model weight should move to reduce loss.
A gradual rise from tiny model updates at the start of training.
A small pressure against unnecessarily large model-weight changes.
Small trainable matrices attached to a frozen model so that only a small share of its numbers must be updated.
One fresh RL attempt at a task.
The numeric result used for RL; the simplest form is 1 for a verified solve and 0 for a genuine, correctly graded failure.
An RL method that compares several attempts at the same task. It can train without learning a separate estimate of expected future reward.

An older RL method that normally learns an extra estimate of expected future reward. That estimate may be a small added output on the main model or a separate model, and it adds memory and complexity.
A version of GRPO designed to stop long answers from receiving unintended extra influence.
A GRPO variant that seeks task groups with useful reward differences and treats long responses more carefully.
An RL method that limits changes to a whole generated answer rather than each generated token separately.
A cost for moving too far from the model that RL started from.
A limit on how much one update can change the probability of an action.
An optional reward for keeping the model output varied.
A control for how varied fresh model output is; higher values make attempts less predictable.
A probability cutoff; top-p 0.9 keeps the smallest set of next tokens whose probabilities add to 90%.
The share of tasks solved with one attempt.
The share of tasks solved at least once in four attempts.
A recorded random-number starting point; several seeds show how much luck affects a result.
A controlled comparison in which one planned choice changes and the rest stay fixed.
A common 16-bit number format that uses less memory than ordinary 32-bit numbers during training.
Storing model numbers with fewer bits; it saves memory but can change behavior, so it is a separate experiment.
A deliberately tiny run used to prove a setup works before an expensive run.
A range showing how much a result could change on a different but comparable task sample.
A short digital fingerprint used to prove two files contain the same bytes.
The experiment dashboard used to track training, reward, and run-health measurements without uploading private task content.
One version of an experiment, such as teacher-SFT at one learning rate.
A running copy of the model that accepts requests and returns generated output.

definitions.term: Packaged software image or container image
definitions.meaning: A fixed bundle of code and software libraries used to run a job the same way again.
A planned order for showing training examples, such as basic investigation actions before complete solutions.
One graphics processor used for one hour.
One task website kept running for one hour.
One of the repository's two software systems for running RL. It generates task attempts, gets scores from the task grader, and uses those scores to update the model.
The repository's other software system for running RL. It serves the same broad purpose as Miles, so the first comparison should give both systems the same model, tasks, budgets, and update settings.
A compact way to write a small number; 1e-6 means 0.000001.

sequence.title: 1. Freeze fair measurement
sequence.detail: Choose one primary agent-software setup, prove a valid base-model evaluation, and lock the approved tasks, splits, graders, budgets, and broken-run rule.

sequence.title: 2. Find the best SFT examples
sequence.detail: At one middle-of-the-road training setting, compare teacher traces, Qwen traces, and a 50:50 mixture measured by trained tokens. Compare training every eligible action with a task-balanced set of key actions, and repeat on split A and split B.

sequence.title: 3. Tune SFT updates
sequence.detail: For the two best data approaches, combine learning rates 3e-7, 1e-6, and 3e-6 with global batches 8, 32, and 64. Compare checkpoints after 1, 2, and 4 epochs, then repeat finalists three times with different random seeds.

sequence.title: 4. Prove RL gets real learning signal
sequence.detail: Run one-update Miles and SkyRL canaries with one training task and eight attempts. Continue only if the real grader produces useful reward differences, the model updates, a checkpoint saves, and that checkpoint reloads.

sequence.title: 5. Choose the RL starting model
sequence.detail: With identical tasks and attempt settings, compare RL from the base model, best teacher SFT, best self SFT, and best mixed SFT for ten updates.

sequence.title: 6. Tune the working RL path
sequence.detail: Vary RL learning rate, attempts per task, distance penalty, update limits, and task sampling in that order. Increase from 10 to 50 updates only after development improvement, and to 100–150 only after stable medium runs.

sequence.title: 7. Test frozen finalists
sequence.detail: Compare base, SFT-only, RL-from-base, and SFT-then-RL with three independent training runs each. Freeze the winners before opening the final Fleet tasks and any external benchmark reserved for final reporting.

decisions.meaning: The exact bytes of Qwen3.8-27B before training. Never compare against a model that merely has the same display name.
values: Exact saved model version 1d4bf0f2... and its locked file hashes

decisions.meaning: The rules that turn text and tool calls into model tokens. A formatting change can alter tool use by itself.
values: The exact files locked with the base model

decisions.meaning: How precisely weights are stored and computed. A smaller numerical format is a separate experiment.
values: BF16 (the defined 16-bit format) for the Qwen runs described here
do not silently store weights with fewer bits

decisions.meaning: The agent program around Qwen. A harness comparison requires a fresh base and trained result under each harness.
values: Qwen Code and OpenCode are two separate experiment blocks. Choose one primary harness

decisions.meaning: The exact source and packaged software image for the agent program. “OpenCode” or “Qwen Code” without a version is not enough.
values: One version that cannot change after publication per experiment block

decisions.meaning: The instructions and actions available to the agent. Tool definitions must be enforced by the running system, not only described in text.
values: The task's exact instructions, command tool, and final-report tool (internally named bash and submit_report)

decisions.meaning: Whether an overlong conversation is summarized and then continued. First prove that a shortened run really continues. Never call a context failure a model failure.
values: Off, or one proven summarize-and-continue policy

decisions.meaning: Maximum time, turns, and tokens allowed for an evaluation attempt. Longer budgets often improve scores without training.
values: One frozen budget derived from successful training-only traces
apply it to base and trained models

decisions.meaning: How random evaluation output is. Use the same values for both arms.
values: One frozen temperature, probability cutoff, and seed policy

decisions.meaning: The exact challenge, its starting state, and the program that scores it. Missing or mismatched grading is an infrastructure failure, not a zero.
values: Version identifiers that cannot change after publication, plus file hashes

decisions.meaning: What happens when a task website, model service, or grader breaks. Apply the same rule to every experiment arm.
values: Preserve the attempt, mark it invalid, and retry only under a rule written before results are seen

decisions.meaning: Which challenges count as real tasks rather than broken infrastructure. A genuine failed solve is eligible; an infrastructure failure is not.
values: Only tasks with a demonstrated working environment, working grader, clean cleanup, and complete current launch information

decisions.meaning: What stays together when tasks are divided. Never split individual windows or attempts at random.
values: Entire task family, including all versions and sessions

decisions.meaning: A different representative assignment of task families. The final 10 stay untouched; compare sensitivity across the two train/development assignments.
values: Existing split A and split B, each 59/20/10

decisions.meaning: The mix of products or web applications. Report both task-level and application-level results.
values: Match the available application proportions, or give each application equal total weight

decisions.meaning: The mix of easier and harder tasks. Do not invent difficulty from test outcomes.
values: Representative natural mix versus equalized easy/medium/hard weight, but only when difficulty labels are independently verified

decisions.meaning: The mix of underlying bug types. Current opaque names are not a trustworthy classification of security weaknesses.
values: Representative mix versus equal family weight, once reliable labels exist

decisions.meaning: How often each training task is selected. Uniform-by-family is the clean baseline.
values: favor tasks that are neither almost always solved nor almost always failed, based only on training results

decisions.meaning: Whether tasks with many saved successes dominate SFT. Measure the mix by supervised tokens as well as trace count.
values: At most 1, 2, or 4 traces per task family

decisions.meaning: The order in which training examples are shown. The current pool has 82 medium, 6 hard, and 1 easy task, so it cannot support a meaningful easy-to-hard comparison.
values: initial exploration and tool-use actions before complete solution chains

decisions.meaning: How quickly complete solutions enter after action-focused examples. Keep total examples and update count matched.
Whether old but still valid task versions remain in training. Never let versions cross task-family splits.
values: Latest valid version only versus all version-compatible training traces

decisions.meaning: How much approved training signal is used. This reveals whether quality, diversity, or raw quantity limits lift.
values: 25%, 50%, and 100% of task families, selected with the same representative sampler

decisions.area: 3. Teacher traces, Qwen traces, and their mixture
decisions.meaning: Which model produced the successful trace. Record exact source-model identity.

decisions.area: 3. Teacher traces, Qwen traces, and their mixture
decisions.meaning: Whether different strong models teach different behavior. Do not let one teacher win merely because it contributed more tokens.
values: Grok-only when enough valid examples exist

decisions.area: 3. Teacher traces, Qwen traces, and their mixture
decisions.meaning: The share of SFT target tokens from strong models versus Qwen. Define the ratio by supervised tokens, not file rows.

decisions.area: 3. Teacher traces, Qwen traces, and their mixture
decisions.meaning: Which saved attempts can teach the model. Never train SFT on a broken, ambiguous, truncated, or merely “completed” attempt.

decisions.area: 3. Teacher traces, Qwen traces, and their mixture
decisions.meaning: How similar accepted examples may be. Preserve uncommon successful strategies while stopping one repeated pattern from dominating.
values: choose a varied capped subset per task

decisions.area: 3. Teacher traces, Qwen traces, and their mixture
decisions.meaning: Whether shorter successful solutions get extra weight. A strong shortest-only filter can teach brittle shortcuts.
values: mild preference among equally correct traces

decisions.area: 3. Teacher traces, Qwen traces, and their mixture
decisions.meaning: Generate new Qwen attempts, keep verified successes, fine-tune, then repeat. Freeze each round and evaluate before using its outputs in the next.
values: Zero, one, or two generate-filter-train rounds

decisions.area: 3. Teacher traces, Qwen traces, and their mixture
decisions.meaning: Whether genuine failures are used as negative examples. Next-token imitation of failures teaches failure.
values: consider only in a separately defined preference or RL objective

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: Which assistant actions contribute to the loss that updates the model. Training every eligible action is the recommended baseline.
values: Every eligible assistant action exactly once
final action only as a health-check comparison
key actions selected by rules written before training

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: Earlier text shown to the model but not learned as a target. The model should learn its actions, not copy server output or secrets.
values: User text, tool output, and copied earlier assistant text receive zero training loss

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: The maximum tokens in one SFT row. Re-tokenize with the exact Qwen tokenizer.

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: How much of the window is reserved for information before the target action. Longer context may help planning but reduces the number of target tokens per batch.

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: Whether a row teaches one action or several nearby actions. Total target-token exposure must remain equal.

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: Where the action appears in the window. Never split a tool call or its immediate result.
values: Place the target action at the end
retain complete tool calls and their boundaries

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: Whether discovery, exploitation, and final reporting receive equal influence. Avoid a training set dominated by the short final submission step.

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: Whether a long trace receives more total influence simply because it has more actions. Equal total weight per task family is the safest primary baseline.

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: How loops and repeated commands are treated. Preserve recovery behavior, not mechanical loops.

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: What happens when a complete action and required context do not fit. Never silently cut tokens and pretend the example is intact.
values: use a larger window in a separate experiment arm

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: Whether attempts containing an automatic conversation summary may enter SFT. A summary is not the original conversation.
values: Exclude unless the conversation before and after the summary can be reconstructed exactly
then compare as a separate data group

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: How much command output is retained as context. No hidden cutting.
values: 16,000 or 50,000 characters per tool result, always keeping the beginning and end and recording every cut

decisions.area: 4. Turning long traces into SFT examples
decisions.meaning: How strongly each source type affects the update. Log the realized weights, not only requested ratios.
values: teacher:self weights matching the declared mixture

decisions.meaning: Update size. Too low learns little; too high damages useful behavior. The repository default is 3e-6; the successful historical run used 1e-6.
values: 1e-5 only as a brief high-risk test

decisions.meaning: Number of SFT windows combined per update across all GPUs. Also log supervised target tokens per update because windows have different lengths.
Rows processed at once by each GPU before update signals are combined. This should not change the scientific result when global batch stays fixed, but it can cause small rounding differences.
How many complete passes are made over SFT rows. Evaluate saved checkpoints inside each run; do not assume the last epoch is best.
The actual amount of assistant output learned from. Equal row counts are not equal training doses.
values: report exact count per epoch and overall

decisions.meaning: Whether update size stays constant or decreases. Current supported path is constant.
values: a smooth decrease from the peak to 10% of the peak

decisions.meaning: A gradual rise from a tiny update size at the start. Current supported path uses 0%; the alternatives are SFT hypotheses, not values copied from an RL study.
A small pressure against very large weight changes. First expose and lock the value the training program actually uses.
A limit on unusually large update signals. Log how often the limit activates.
values: disabled only as a health check

decisions.meaning: Update all model weights or only small attached trainable matrices. The two methods have different learning capacity and model-saving paths.
values: low-rank adapters as a lower-cost comparison

decisions.meaning: Random order of SFT rows. One seed is enough for coarse rejection, not a final claim.
values: At least 3 recorded seeds for finalists

decisions.meaning: How often recoverable model state is saved. It should not change learning, but enables fair checkpoint selection and recovery.
Which saved point becomes the candidate model. Do not choose from prediction error on held-out teacher text, the final Fleet tasks, or WebExploitBench.
values: Highest success on the Fleet development tasks
use training loss only to detect broken or unstable learning

decisions.meaning: The model RL begins from. This directly tests whether SFT is a useful RL warm start.
Tasks on which fresh RL attempts may run. Bind exact task and grader versions.
values: The same training families used by the corresponding SFT arm

decisions.meaning: Which system decides success. A missing scoring ID makes the attempt invalid, not zero reward.
values: The real grader locked to that exact task version, plus a unique ID for each scoring run

decisions.meaning: Reward for the final task result. Binary reward is easiest to audit.
values: verified partial progress in a separate later arm

decisions.meaning: Credit for verified intermediate objectives. Use only progress confirmed by the grader, never a model's self-claim.
values: exact fraction provided by the grader
a separately studied blend only after the fraction is audited

decisions.meaning: Extra credit for calling the final report tool correctly. A large format bonus can teach reporting without exploitation.
values: at most a small separately logged bonus later

decisions.meaning: What happens when the environment, model service, or grader breaks. Do not turn infrastructure failures into negative model feedback.
values: Exclude from model updates and preserve the reason

decisions.meaning: What happens when an otherwise healthy attempt reaches its declared time, turn, or token limit. Track time-limit rate alongside reward.
values: Count it as a genuine model failure under the prewritten rule
mark it invalid only when infrastructure, rather than the model, caused the timeout

decisions.meaning: Whether attempts at one task include both successes and failures. Ordinary GRPO learns nothing from all-zero or all-one groups.
values: Require and log mixed-reward groups in the canary

decisions.meaning: How groups with identical rewards are handled. Record every replacement because it changes which tasks training sees.
values: Keep them and produce zero update as the baseline
later compare a fixed, prewritten replacement cap that seeks useful reward differences

decisions.meaning: Which training task is attempted next. Use training outcomes only.
values: favor tasks that are neither near 0% nor near 100% solved

decisions.meaning: Whether previously generated attempts are reused. Old attempts were generated by an older model and can bias updates.
values: No replay for the primary fresh-attempt run

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: The training system that coordinates generation and updates. Do not treat one system merely starting as evidence of learning.
values: Miles and SkyRL, first as matched one-step canaries

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: The rule that converts rewards into weight updates. Each algorithm needs its own verified implementation.
values: Dr. GRPO, DAPO-style GRPO, and GSPO later
PPO only if its extra expected-reward estimate and added complexity are justified

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Number of fresh responses compared for the same task. Larger groups improve the chance of mixed rewards but cost more website time.
values: 4 only when enough tasks combine into a total batch that divides evenly across all training GPUs

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Number of distinct task prompts contributing to one update. More tasks reduce dependence on one challenge.
values: 1, 2, 4, 8. Start with 1×8 for the canary, then 4×8 if speed allows

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Update size for reward-based training. Several open GRPO recipes use 1e-6, but math tasks are not cyber agents.
values: 3e-6 only as a brief high-risk test

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: How long RL runs. More updates are not automatically better.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: How many times the same newly generated attempts are reused immediately. Reuse may learn more from each attempt but moves training farther from the model that generated the data.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: The fixed model used to measure how far RL moves. Log the exact reference checkpoint.
values: periodic reference reset only in a later long-run study

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Strength of the cost for moving away from the reference model. Track the measured change, not only the requested number.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Maximum change in action probability trusted in one update. The repository's Miles path already names the 0.2/0.28 shape.
values: Equal lower and upper limits of 0.2
DAPO-style lower limit 0.2 and upper limit 0.28

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Whether long and short attempts receive equal total weight or equal weight per token. Track response length because ordinary GRPO can favor long incorrect output.
values: Dr. GRPO adjustment that removes unintended extra weight from long answers

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: An optional reward for keeping output varied. Use only if diversity collapses; too much produces noise.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Randomness while collecting training attempts. Evaluation temperature remains fixed separately.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: How much of the model's token distribution remains available. “Top-p 0.9” keeps the smallest token set whose probabilities add to 90%.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Maximum prompt plus generated tokens in one attempt. Any cutting caused by the limit must be reported.
values: 65,536 and 98,304. Start with the reviewed 98,304-token limit

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Portion of total context available for model generation. It must remain below the total budget.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Maximum generated tokens before the next tool call or observation. A too-small turn cap can prevent complete commands or reports.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Maximum model/tool cycles in one attempt. Use enough room to finish, then study efficiency.
values: 120 only if successful training-only traces justify it

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Real-time deadline for one full attempt. Base the choice on valid training-only completion times.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Maximum time for one command. Client timeout must exceed the advertised tool timeout.
values: At least 330 seconds for a five-minute server limit

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Maximum command-result text returned to the model. Mark any cut clearly and use the same rule in every attempt.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: How current the attempt-producing model is relative to the training model. An unlimited delay trains on behavior from an old model.
values: Refresh it after every model update first
allow at most one-update delay later

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Whether fresh attempts and model training share GPUs. This should mainly affect computing speed, but confirm that rounding and model-update timing remain comparable.
values: separate them only for a matched speed study

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: How often RL saves and checks development tasks. Keep the best and latest recoverable states.

decisions.area: 7. RL attempts, model updates, and running system
decisions.meaning: Whether a stopped run continues from the exact next task/update. Restore weights, optimizer, random state, and data position together.
values: One planned stop-and-resume test before a long run

decisions.meaning: The ordered stages applied to Qwen. These are the core scientific arms.
Whether imitation gives RL a better starting success rate. Match the RL task mix, number of attempts, and number of model updates.
Whether a final imitation pass restores format or tool behavior. It can erase RL gains, so evaluate both sides.
Switch between SFT and RL more than once. Freeze and evaluate every boundary.
Mix non-cyber instruction data to reduce forgetting. Non-cyber data is outside the current goal and must not be mixed into its main result.
values: 5% or 10% only in a clearly separate follow-up study

decisions.meaning: Move the KL reference to a newer checkpoint. ProRL motivates studying this for long runs, not using it by default.
The result used to choose recipes. Training loss and prediction error on teacher-written text are health checks, not the target.
values: Fleet development pass@1, averaged equally across task families

decisions.meaning: Other useful views of capability. Label them secondary before running.
values: pass@4, verified partial progress, application-average success, completion time, turns, and tokens

decisions.meaning: The untouched score reported after selection. Open once per frozen finalist family. With only 10 tasks, treat small differences as uncertain.
A separate test of improvement beyond Fleet tasks. If its results help choose data, settings, or checkpoints, it is a development test—not independent final evidence.
values: A newly validated, fair WebExploitBench comparison used only for reporting
reserve another untouched benchmark if WebExploitBench results influence choices

decisions.meaning: Whether lift survives a different agent program. A trained-versus-base comparison is required inside each harness.
values: Primary harness result, then a separately matched Qwen Code/OpenCode pair

decisions.meaning: Number of tries per task. Never rerun a valid pass@1 zero.
How often training pauses for task evaluation. The development tasks must never enter training, and frequent repeated checks can overfit decisions to them.
values: run the full Fleet development test after each completed training run
for very long runs, optionally use one fixed small development subset at epoch or stage boundaries

decisions.meaning: Independent training runs with different seeds. Evaluation attempts are not substitutes for training repeats.
Compare base and trained outcomes on the same task versions. Do not compare only two pooled percentages.
values: Per-task win/loss/tie table and a paired resampling confidence interval: repeatedly resample whole task families and recalculate the lift

decisions.meaning: A range showing sampling uncertainty. Attempts on one task are related, not independent data points.
values: Repeatedly resample whole task families, not individual attempts

decisions.choice: Guard against a lucky search winner
decisions.meaning: Avoid declaring the luckiest of many recipes a discovery. Report the number of experiment arms tried.
values: Write down the search before it starts, use development data for ranking, and reserve the final test for a small frozen set

decisions.meaning: Smallest improvement worth the cost. With only 10 final tasks, only very large changes will be clear.
values: Write down the minimum absolute increase in task success before running the search

decisions.meaning: Resources needed for each gain. The best model is not necessarily the most expensive winner.
values: GPU-hours, environment-hours, generated tokens, and solved tasks per cost

decisions.meaning: Check whether cyber lift damages basic tool use or reporting. Keep this separate from the cyber success score.
values: Fixed small test set for non-secret tool formatting and general instructions

decisions.meaning: Hash every model, tokenizer, and conversation-format file.
Hash the task list, split, list of saved source attempts, prepared rows, and source weights actually used.
Record the exact saved code version, packaged software image, full settings, seed, GPU layout, and intended update count.
Record exact task, environment, grader, tools, and one unique grader execution ID per RL attempt.
Record checkpoint, model-service image, agent software, task and grader versions, budgets, seeds, and retry policy.
Send training loss, reward, update size, output length, invalid-attempt rate, task mix, and checkpoint details to Weights & Biases, the experiment dashboard. Never upload prompts or traces.
Save model, optimizer, learning-rate state, the exact state of the random sequence, and the exact next data position. Test one stop and resume.
Reload the exported model and prove it can produce numeric predictions without invalid numbers before using it for evaluation.
Separate “program started,” “model updated,” “valid score produced,” and “model improved.” They are different claims.
